summary: The iPad resets the user reported are real and systemic. Every applied cloud state (clean pull, three-way merge, and the push that loses its compare-and-set race because another device pushed first) ends in cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() -> KOS.rerender(), which fully remounts #main with no check of what changed or whether the user is mid-task; the only guard is the ink pen (1.5 s). Pulls fire on Realtime notes from any other device, on every return to the app (visibility/focus) and after the iPad's own ratings, so redraws are frequent. A remount loses everything held in render closures: the CS/Maths/IT note page (the study spaces store theirs and survive), the flashcard queue and session counts (the batch is logged only at finish, so pay/streak for ratings before the redraw is lost), quiz and exam progress and typed answers, Japanese session results, Code listing edits and retrieval tries/hints/clock, open menus, focus/keyboard, and scroll: rerender saves #main.scrollTop but #stage is the real scroller, so every redraw jumps to the top on all three devices, and Side by side panes reset too. The same blanket KOS.rerender is used as a change broadcast by the Daily Review close, routine auto-ticks and boot loaders, while Google/Todoist pulls refresh nothing. Fix design: a redraw policy (background changes carry the changed keys; views declare what they read; redraws are deferred while a dialog/menu/editable focus/active study engine/recent interaction exists, with a quiet Refresh chip), per-view transient state kept per device in state.ui as the Code/Japanese/Mind/Creatives lesson pages already do, partial review batches banked on unmount, and rerender preserving the real scroller, pane scrolls and focus.
coverage: Read the redraw paths in js/core/ui.js (KOS.rerender, KOS.show), cloudsync.js (every rerenderCurrent caller, Realtime, visibility/focus/interval, the CAS conflict path), routines.js, dayreview.js, ext.js, main.js, achievements, focus, mobile-shell, the ink listeners, and the engines (flashcards, quiz, jarun, Code retrieval, the codetopic/jatopic/crtopic/mindtopic page memos). Reproduced with KOS.rerender() (exactly what cloudsync calls) on the seeded account at ipad, ipadl, mac and iphone: notes page, flashcards (topic and Due today), quiz, exam typed answer, Code 1.1 listings, quick-note focus, bell menu, assignment dialog focus, Daily Review close, Side by side ink panes, scroll on topic/Home/Anime; toast geometry on iphone and ipad. Screenshots: shots/sync-disruption/review-close-notes-reset.png, shots/sync-disruption/toast-over-rate-iphone.png. NOT reproduced end to end: a real two-device Supabase pull (no cloud sign-in in the harness; the chain is code-read), a routine auto-tick redraw (a hand-made ledger entry did not tick a habit), a Japanese session with due items (none due in the sample), the Creatives Writing Desk (autosaves at 600 ms), the Focus stage and exam paper tally (overlays outside #main, judged safe from code). The empty account was not exercised separately: with no cloud link it has no pull-triggered redraws and the remount behaviour is identical. Themes are not relevant to this area and were not checked.

findings.title: KOS.rerender() never keeps the scroll position: it saves #main.scrollTop but #stage is the scroller, so every cloud pull jumps the page to the top
findings.detail: KOS.rerender (the cloud-pull/background redraw path) reads and restores document.getElementById('main').scrollTop, but the element that actually scrolls is #stage (#main has overflow visible; on the iPad #main.scrollHeight 2406 vs #stage 2406/1120 scrolling). KOS.show then empties #main, the height collapses and the browser clamps #stage.scrollTop to 0. Repro (seeded account): open compsci 4.5.2.1, set #stage.scrollTop=900, KOS.rerender() -> 0. Same on Home (700 -> 0) and the Anime vault (1500 -> 0) at mac, ipad and iphone sizes. So any pull, merge, auto-ticked habit, Daily Review close etc. throws the reader back to the top of the page.
findings.evidence: harness eval sd3.js: ipad {st1:900,st2:0,h1:700,h2:0,a1:1500,a2:0}; mac {st1:530,st2:0,...}; iphone same. Code: js/core/ui.js:353-356 (var main=getElementById('main'); var top=main.scrollTop; ... main.scrollTop=top); KOS.show resets main.scrollTop=0 at js/core/ui.js:1526
findings.fix: Save/restore the real scroller (#stage, or a KOS.shell.scroller() helper that returns the element whose overflow scrolls, including the phone shell) and restore AFTER the view has rendered (and once more after async content lands, e.g. on next rAF / after vault lazy batch). Better: part of the redraw policy below — background redraws should not happen while the user is reading.
findings.rootCause: rerender measured the wrong element after the shell moved scrolling to #stage

findings.title: CS/Maths/IT notes reset to page 1 on every background redraw (the reported 'notes page 4 jumps back to page 1')
findings.detail: In a subject topic the current note page lives in a closure variable (`var notePage = 0` inside the topic view). KOS.rerender re-runs the view, so the variable is recreated at 0. hub.js keeps only the open TAB across a redraw (openTabMemo), not the page. Repro on iPad: open compsci 4.5.2.1, Next page x3 -> 'Page 4 of 7', KOS.rerender() -> 'Page 1 of 7'. Code, Japanese, Mind and Creatives lessons do NOT have this bug because they store the page in state.ui.<space>.page[ref].
findings.evidence: harness eval: {before:'Page 4 of 7', after:'Page 1 of 7'} at --size ipad. js/modules/hub.js:2901 (var notePage = 0), :2983 (cur = o.keep ? notePage : 0), :2590 (only the tab survives KOS.ui.redrawing). Contrast js/modules/codetopic.js:342/377, jatopic.js:206/229, crtopic.js:154/171, mindtopic.js:261/282 (ui.page[ref])
findings.fix: Keep the note page in a module-level memo keyed by sid:ref (like openTabMemo) or per device in state.ui.notePage[sid:ref], and read it when KOS.ui.redrawing (and arguably on return to the topic). Same pattern the study spaces already use.
findings.rootCause: transient reader state held in a view-render closure

findings.title: A background redraw mid-flashcards restarts the set at card 1 and silently drops the cards already rated from the session ledger (no XP, no streak credit)
findings.detail: The flashcard engine keeps queue, graduated and counts in its mount closure, and only logs the review session in finish(). A KOS.rerender mid-set remounts it: on a topic's Flashcards tab the queue is rebuilt from ALL the topic's cards, so the learner is put back on card 1 and re-meets cards they just rated (re-rating them applies FSRS's short-term rule again, skewing their schedule); on Due today the counts reset ('This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good' -> ''), and because a session is only logged at finish(), the ratings made before the redraw never produce a session entry — their XP/gold and the study-streak credit are lost (the SRS schedule itself was saved). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Flashcards, rate 3 Good ('15 left of 18'), KOS.rerender() -> '18 left of 18', first card again. Due today: rate 3 ('304 left of 307', life line 3 good) -> after rerender '304 left of 304', life line empty.
findings.evidence: harness eval (ipad): topic log ['18 left of 18 What is a number base?', ..., '15 left of 18'] -> afterFront '18 left of 18 What is a number base?'; due {d3life:'This session: 0 again · 0 hard · 3 good · 0 easy', dAfterLife:''}. js/engines/flashcards.js:295-322 (rate keeps counts in closure, store.save only), :325-355 (finish is the only KOS.sessions.log), :356 restart
findings.fix: (1) Never redraw under an active study session (redraw policy below). (2) Keep an in-progress review session in a per-device session store (state.ui.fcSession[deckKey] = {queue keys, graduated, counts, startedAt}) and resume it on remount. (3) Log/bank the partial batch on unmount/pagehide (like Focus banks its clock, invariant 4c) so pay never depends on the DOM surviving.
findings.rootCause: session progress and the pay-at-finish rule live in DOM-bound closures

findings.title: Quiz progress and a typed exam answer are wiped by any background redraw
findings.detail: Topic Quiz (MCQ) and Exam tabs keep the question index, chosen answers and typed text in engine closures. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.2.1 Quiz, answer two -> 'Question 3 of 11'; KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 11' (tab kept, progress lost). Exam tab: go to 'Question 3 of 14', type into the answer textarea, KOS.rerender() -> 'Question 1 of 14' and the textarea is empty: the typed answer is lost with no recovery.
findings.evidence: harness eval sd1.js (ipad): {quizBefore:'Question 3 of 11', quizAfter:'Question 1 of 11', examBefore:'Question 3 of 14', examTA:true, examAfter:'Question 1 of 14', examTAAfter:''}. js/engines/quiz.js:62-121 (MCQ state in closure), :225-232 (exam 'at' index in closure); js/modules/hub.js:3044-3084 remounts them
findings.fix: Persist the quiz/exam position and drafts per device (state.ui.quizRun[sid:ref] = {at, picks, drafts}) like Code drafts, and restore on remount; plus the redraw policy (no background redraw while a study engine is mounted and touched).
findings.rootCause: engine state in closures + unconditional rerender

findings.title: Every cloud pull/merge redraws the active view unconditionally — even when nothing the view shows changed, and even while the user is mid-task
findings.detail: cloudsync.rerenderCurrent() calls KOS.rerender() after every applied remote state: the clean path (applyRemoteState, cloudsync.js:775), the merge path (mergeRemoteIn, :495, also used by a push that lost its compare-and-set race, :533-560) and first link (:1279). There is no check of whether the merged document differs in anything the current view reads, no check that the user is interacting, a dialog/menu is open, an input has focus, or a study engine is running. The only guard in KOS.rerender is the ink pen (ui.js:347). Triggers that reach it: another device's push -> Realtime 'changed' (1.5 s debounce, :1483); returning to the app (visibilitychange/focus, :1548-1552, at most once a minute) — on the iPad every app switch; the 15-min interval; and the iPad's OWN ratings: each store.save -> noteChange -> push after 4 s -> if the Mac/iPhone pushed meanwhile the CAS fails -> conflict() -> mergeRemoteIn -> rerender. An idle open Mac pushes on its own (achievement sweep every 30 min, goals/notify ticks, routine auto-ticks, Daily Review words), so the iPad is redrawn under the user regularly. This is the root of the reported iPad resets.
findings.evidence: js/core/cloudsync.js:487-497 (mergeRemoteIn -> rerenderCurrent), :723-733 (rerenderCurrent -> KOS.rerender), :773-777, :533-560 (conflict path), :1447-1459 (noteChange push), :1480-1495 (Realtime), :1541-1553 (interval/visible/focus); js/core/ui.js:344-357 (rerender: only inkUI.busy guard). Harness: KOS.rerender() reproduces every reset in the other findings.
findings.fix: Systemic redraw policy: (1) cloudsync passes what changed (top-level keys that differ between pre- and post-merge state, cheap JSON compare per key) to KOS.rerender({changed:[...], background:true}); views declare the state keys they read (KOS.views.x.reads = ['srs','edits',...]) and are skipped when untouched. (2) A background redraw is DEFERRED while the page is 'busy': a dialog or menu open, focus in an input/textarea/contenteditable, a study engine mounted and touched in the last N minutes (flashcards/quiz/exam/japanese session/code task), pointer down, or within 30 s of the last interaction — instead show a quiet 'Updated on another device · Refresh' chip, and redraw on the next navigation. (3) For views that must refresh live, give them a refresh(changed) hook that patches in place instead of a full remount.
findings.devices: iPad primarily (app switching + Pencil study), all
findings.rootCause: full remount used as the generic refresh for background state changes, with no busy/changed gating

findings.title: Closing the Daily Review sheet (Later, Esc, Close) redraws the page underneath — and on the iPad it can auto-open over a lesson when you return to the app
findings.detail: reviewSheet.close() calls KOS.rerender() whenever it is not silent (dayreview.js:92), as does the final Close button (:661) and Skip (:709). The overlay is outside #main, so the page under it never needed a redraw; the redraw resets notes page, flashcards, quiz, scroll. Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3 notes page 4 ('Page 4 of 7'), KOS.reviewSheet.open(slot), close -> 'Page 1 of 7' (screenshot). Worse, maybeOpen() runs on every visibilitychange to visible (:749); the deep-link guard uses bootHash, which is cleared 1.5 s after boot (:746), so after boot the sheet auto-opens over ANY page (a topic, a Code lesson, Due today) when the iPad app is brought back inside a new review slot; the blocked() check knows only Focus, a dialog and the Exam Room. Dismissing it then wipes the lesson state.
findings.evidence: shots/sync-disruption/review-close-notes-reset.png (Page 1 of 7 after close; was Page 4 of 7). eval sd8.js {before:'Page 4 of 7', open:true, after:'Page 1 of 7'}. js/modules/dayreview.js:85-93, :661, :709, :722-729 (blocked), :744-749
findings.fix: Close should repaint only what the review changed (chip, Home's cards if Home is on screen) — or call the policy's refresh(changed) — never a full remount. Auto-open on visibility should only happen on Home (or when no study page/engine is active); elsewhere it waits in the chip.
findings.rootCause: overlay close uses KOS.rerender as a blanket refresh; auto-open guard only considers boot deep links

findings.title: Handwritten tab Side by side: both panes jump to the top on a background redraw (1.5 s after the pen lifts)
findings.detail: The ink guard in KOS.rerender only waits while inkUI.busy() (a stroke or text box open, or ink in the last 1.5 s). Once the pen has been lifted for 1.5 s — i.e. while the student reads the notes pane or thinks — a pull redraws the tab and both independent scroll regions reset. Repro iPad landscape (1180x820): compsci 4.5.4.3, Handwritten, Side by side; ink.side-notes scrolled to 600 and ink.side-page to 238; KOS.rerender() -> both 0. The notebook page-in-view and the notes position are lost, exactly the 'jumps back to the start' symptom on the iPad.
findings.evidence: eval sd11.js (ipadl): {scrollers:['ink.side-notes 7882/744','ink.side-page 982/744'], before:[600,238], after:['ink.side-notes 0','ink.side-page 0']}. js/core/ui.js:347-351 (busy guard only), js/core/inkui.js:341
findings.fix: Remember scroll of every [data-scroll-keep]/pane scroller (extend noteScrolls, ui.js:686, to vertical scrollTop for declared panes) and restore after render; better, defer background redraws while the Handwritten tab is open at all (ink pages and notes never change from a state pull — inksync updates pages itself).
findings.devices: iPad landscape (Side by side is >1080 only)
findings.rootCause: rerender only preserves horizontal scroller memos and the (wrong) #main scrollTop

findings.title: A background redraw steals focus from whatever is being typed in — the iPad/iPhone keyboard closes mid-sentence
findings.detail: KOS.rerender remounts #main; the focused field is destroyed and focus falls to <body>. The quick-note draft itself survives (stored per device), but the caret is gone, so on the iPad the on-screen keyboard dismisses while the user is typing; any keystrokes in flight are lost. The same applies to every inline input on any page (search filters in vaults, Money amount fields, Goals editor in-page fields, Code task editor, Writing Desk). Repro iPad: compsci 4.5.4.3, focus the quick note, type, caret at 4, KOS.rerender() -> document.activeElement BODY; the new textarea has the text but no focus (selection at end).
findings.evidence: eval (ipad): {active:'BODY ', val:'half a thou', sel:11}. js/core/ui.js:344-357, :1520-1541 (main.innerHTML = '' then remount); js/core/a11y.js:97 comment says a redraw must leave the reader where they are but there is no focus restore
findings.fix: Policy: never run a background redraw while document.activeElement is an editable element inside #main (defer until blur + idle). As a fallback, record a focus signature (data-ui + index + selection) before the redraw and restore it after (mobile-shell.js:600-640 already has calendarFocusSignature to generalise).

findings.title: Japanese review/learn session restarts and loses its unlogged results on a background redraw
findings.detail: KOS.jaRun.run keeps `results` and the index in its closure and pays only at the end (KOS.ja.finishSession(results)). A KOS.rerender on #/japanese/session/... re-runs run(): the list is rebuilt from KOS.ja.due() (facets already graded drop out) and the results so far are discarded, so the +1 XP per passed facet for them is never logged. Mind's Daily 15 does it right: its d.results are saved in state and logged once (mind.js:594/662).
findings.evidence: js/modules/jarun.js:361-390 (run, `var results = [], i = 0`), :434 (finishSession only at end); js/modules/japanese.js:305 (view calls run on every render); contrast js/modules/mind.js:594,662
findings.fix: Keep the running session (keys, index, results) per device in state.ui.japanese.run and resume on remount, or bank results incrementally; plus the redraw policy.
findings.rootCause: session state in closure + pay at finish

findings.title: A background redraw closes any open menu or popover — including the header bell, which is outside the page
findings.detail: KOS.show always calls closeOpenMenu(false) before drawing, also for a redraw (_nav). So a pull arriving while the notifications popover, a Filters menu or a ⋯ menu is open makes it vanish under the finger. Repro: Home, open the bell (menu .k-menu-panel.k-nt-pop present), KOS.rerender() -> menu gone.
findings.evidence: eval sd6.js (ipad): {menuOpen:true, menuCls:'k-menu-panel k-nt-pop', menuAfter:false}. js/core/ui.js:1513-1519 (closeOpenMenu before every render)
findings.fix: On a redraw (KOS.ui.redrawing) keep a menu whose anchor is outside #main, and for menus inside #main defer the background redraw while a menu is open (redraw policy).

findings.title: Edits in a Code lesson's runnable listings are lost on a background redraw
findings.detail: A Code lesson's notes listings are editable (code.editor-input) so the learner can experiment, but their text is not kept anywhere; task editors save drafts (debounced 400 ms, state.ui.code.drafts) and survive. Repro iPad: code 1.1, type into the three listing editors, wait 900 ms, KOS.rerender() -> all three back to the shipped code (the quick-note textarea survives).
findings.evidence: eval sd5.js: {n:4, where:['code.editor-input'x3,'topic.quick-note'], kept:[false,false,false,true]}. js/modules/code.js:629-632 (only tasks call setDraft); js/core/code.js:612-621
findings.fix: Keep listing edits as drafts too (key `listing:<lesson>:<i>`, cleared by 'Reset'), or defer redraws while an editor has focus.
findings.rootCause: listing editor state only in the DOM

findings.title: routines.onSession redraws the whole page whenever an auto-tracked habit ticks itself — e.g. right after a flashcard batch or Code task pass
findings.detail: Every logged session (flashcard batch finish, exam item marked, Code task pass, Japanese session) calls routines.onSession, which runs autoSync() and, if any auto-tracked habit ticked, KOS.rerender() (only guarded against an open dialog). So the moment a 'Review 20 cards' or '1 Code task passed' habit completes, the page that caused it is remounted: the flashcards 'Session complete' summary is replaced by a fresh deck, a Code task's passing result panel is redrawn, an exam tab returns to question 1. Only the habit chip/Home needs to change.
findings.evidence: js/core/routines.js:697-700 (onSession -> autoSync -> KOS.rerender), :672-690 (autoSync), js/engines/flashcards.js:349 (session logged at finish), js/engines/quiz.js:428 (exam item logs a session). Not reproduced end-to-end in the harness (could not get an auto habit to tick with a hand-made ledger entry); path read from code.
findings.fix: Replace the blanket rerender with a 'routines changed' event that Home/Routines/the header chip listen to; never remount a study view for it.

findings.title: Toasts are capped at half the viewport width and, on the iPhone, sit on top of the flashcard rating buttons (and catch taps when they carry Undo)
findings.detail: #toast is positioned with inset-inline-start:50% + translate(-50%), so its shrink-to-fit width is limited to the space right of the centre line: 201 px on the iPhone (402/2) and 410 px on the iPad (820/2). A one-line message wraps to four lines (98 px tall). On the iPhone it sits 12 px above the tab bar, i.e. exactly over the Hard/Good rating buttons of a flashcard (toast 101,708 201x98 vs rate row 16,694 370x60: overlapping), and an action toast has pointer-events:auto, so a rating tap lands on the toast. Flashcards themselves raise toasts mid-set (leech, 'Type your answer first').
findings.evidence: shots/sync-disruption/toast-over-rate-iphone.png; eval sd10.js iphone {toast:[101,708,201,98], rate:[16,694,370,60], overlap:true, pe:'auto'}, ipad {toast:[205,1092,410,64]}. css/components.css:389-408, :669
findings.fix: Centre with inset-inline:0; margin-inline:auto; inline-size:fit-content (keep max-inline-size), and on study pages lift the toast above the active control row (or place it top-centre on phones while a study engine is mounted).
findings.rootCause: left:50% shrink-to-fit width; fixed bottom offset ignores page controls

findings.title: A redraw mid-retrieval resets the Code retrieval card's tries, hint flag and clock, so the derived grade comes out better than earned
findings.detail: Code retrieval grades are derived from tries, hints and time (invariant 107, never self-reported), but the card keeps `started`, `tries` and `hinted` in its render closure. After a failed try and an opened hint, a background redraw remounts the card with tries=0, hinted=false and a fresh clock; passing then records a clean, fast first-try grade and schedules the card too far out. Task timers (code.js:601) reset the same way.
findings.evidence: js/modules/code.js:972 (var started = Date.now(), tries = 0, hinted = false), :984 (clock), :601-611 (task clock). Code-read; the remount path is the same KOS.rerender reproduced in the other findings.
findings.fix: Keep the in-progress attempt (tries, hinted, startedAt) per card in state.ui.code.attempt[key] until it is graded, and defer background redraws while a retrieval is open.

findings.title: After a background redraw the open dialog's opener is detached, so closing it drops focus to <body>
findings.detail: Dialogs survive a redraw (they live on body), but KOS.ui.openDialog restores focus to the opener, which the redraw replaced. Repro: Assignments, '＋ New assignment', type a title, KOS.rerender() (dialog and text survive), Cancel -> document.activeElement is BODY; the keyboard/VoiceOver user is thrown to the top of the document. cloudsync does not check for an open dialog (routines.onSession does).
findings.evidence: eval sd7.js: {dlgAfter:true, inpAfter:'Typed title', openerConnected:false, focusAfterClose:'BODY'}. js/core/routines.js:699 has the dialog guard; js/core/cloudsync.js:723-733 has none
findings.fix: Defer background redraws while KOS.ui.topDialog() (policy), and in openDialog's restore fall back to an element with the same data-ui/text in the new DOM (as mobile-shell's calendarFocusSignature already does, mobile-shell.js:620-640).

findings.title: Boot-time redraws of whatever page the PWA reopened on (Google read-only copy, own art pictures, sample seed)
findings.detail: Three boot paths call KOS.rerender() on the current page after async work: KOS.ext boot when Google Calendar is connected (ext.js:364, after loadRo from IndexedDB), KOS.art.loadOwn (main.js:307) and the sample seed (main.js:299-304). The iPad Home Screen app restores the last route (e.g. a topic), so the page the user has just started reading or tapping is remounted a moment after launch, for data (Google's read-only chips, decorative art) that only Calendar or a painted slot needs.
findings.fix: Have these refresh only the views that read them (Calendar for loadRo; the art slots via KOS.art.apply/paint, which artslot.js already does in place) instead of a full remount.

findings.title: Inconsistent refresh policy: Google/Todoist pulls change Calendar and Reminders without redrawing them, while a state pull redraws every page
findings.detail: KOS.ext.syncAll (every cycle and the 1.5 s 'soon' sync) writes pulled events and reminders through the owners, then only notifies KOS.ext.onChange listeners — only the Connections page listens. An open Calendar or Reminders page keeps showing the old data (a task completed in Todoist stays unticked on screen) until the user navigates, whereas a cloud state pull remounts any page however unrelated. There is no single 'state changed → which views care' mechanism.
findings.evidence: js/core/ext.js:325-337 (syncAll -> changed()), :294; js/modules/connections.js:173-177 (the only listener); js/core/extgcal.js and exttasks.js contain no redraw
findings.fix: Introduce one change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) fired by cloudsync (with the keys that differed), ext, routines, inksync, files; views subscribe by domain and refresh in place (or defer while busy).

qol: Show a quiet 'Updated from another device' chip with Refresh instead of redrawing a busy page
Remember the CS/Maths/IT note page per topic (like the study spaces) so returning to a topic lands where you left off
Keep a partly rated flashcard batch resumable from the Due today chip after leaving the page
backlog: Domain-scoped change bus (KOS.changed(domains)) replacing KOS.rerender as a broadcast; views refresh in place
Per-view session store for transient study state, so engines resume after any remount, reload or iPad app kill
Smoke test: for each study view set transient state, call KOS.rerender(), assert page, card, question, scroll and focus survive
